Checked logical versus physical/compressed byte scopes and catalog, snapshot, manifest, file, row-group, page, block, split, and task identities remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Pruning fractions are explicitly conditional rather than assumed statistically independent.

numerical_recomputation.notes: Figures exclude separately identified metadata, footer, index, delete, cache, compression, false-positive, and request work.

evidence: Checked the conditional product B_total times partition/file/row-group/column retained fractions and its correlation caveat.
Reviewed workload-weighted candidate cost vectors after hard-constraint gating rather than compensating an infeasible dimension through weights.
Checked read/write/metadata/storage amplification, target task/file heuristic, and immutable old/new migration snapshot identities.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The decision framework requires raw evidence and sensitivity analysis rather than one dimensionless opaque score.

evidence: Reviewed zero/sparse/hot/skewed partitions, tiny/large/unsplittable files, row-group/page extremes, wide/nested/high-cardinality data, null/NaN/time-zone/collation behavior, and compression changes.

Reviewed append/update/delete, copy-on-write/merge-on-read, late data, dense delete files, concurrent change during migration, ambiguous commit, cold restore, cache churn, request throttling, and compute/storage scale mismatch.

evidence: Traced stable logical table identity through catalog, schema/spec/sort, snapshot, manifest, exact file version, physical fragments, protection, tier, and lifecycle.
Checked writers publish unique immutable files through conditional snapshot commits and readers pin exact membership.

Checked migration pins source, captures concurrent changes, validates logical/nonfunctional properties, conditionally cuts over, preserves rollback, and delays cleanup until all references and policies release.
invariant_checking.notes: Data, metadata, catalog, keys, policy, and recovery evidence are treated as one recoverable system.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step layout audit from workload/constraint definition through layered candidates, feasibility, modeling, benchmarking, compatibility/protection, decision evidence, migration, cutover, and retirement.

Checked counterexamples for vendor-first selection, average-only workload, universal multiplicative pruning, paths-equal-table, more-partitions-equal-better, Parquet-equal-layout, replicas-equal-backup, warm-cache proof, fastest-candidate selection, and in-place migration.
Reviewed decision durability through assumptions, uncertainty, owner, expiration, rejected alternatives, sensitivity, reevaluation thresholds, canary, and rollback.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external storage architect, query-engine maintainer, table/format maintainer, distributed-filesystem or cloud-provider representative, security auditor, records/privacy/legal specialist, research-ethics authority, accessibility reviewer, or certification review is claimed.
